newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Trelleborg says Boliden sale to fund rubber ops.
newsitem.headline: Trelleborg says Boliden sale to fund rubber ops.

text.p: Swedish mining and rubber company Trelleborg said on Wednesday it would use funds raised through the partial float of its Boliden metals and mining unit in Canada to finance expansion.
"We will use the funds to expand the general business we have in rubber and distribution," company spokesman Leif Oberg told Reuters.
"But we have not released any more details than that and will not do until the company's capital markets day in Visby (Sweden) on June 17."
Trelleborg unveiled plans to spin-off Boliden in Canada in February but said it would retain between 45-49 percent of the unit.
On Wednesday it announced its would sell 51 million shares at C$16 each which would raise Canadian $813 million ($586 million). This values Boliden as a whole at about nine billion crowns.
Boliden will be listed in Toronto and Montreal on June 17.

The issue is being underwritten by a global syndicate led by Nesbitt Burns Inc. It includes Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Morgan Stanley & Co, RBC Dominion Securities Inc, ABN AMRO Rothschild, CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Inc and Scotia McLeod Inc as co-managers.
Oberg said the offer would be made to both institutions and retail clients but he declined to release further details until June 17.
The underwriters have said they expect about 50-60 percent of shares to be sold in Canada and the U.S., 25-30 percent in Europe and the rest in Asia.
Trelleborg has previously said that the float would allow for a "quick and strong expansion" of Boliden's mining operations, primarily in North and South America.
Boliden was taken over by Trelleborg 11 years ago but has not performed very well. It is Trelleborg's biggest unit, accounting for about 40 percent of turnover and half its profits.
-- Belinda Goldsmith, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1017 ($ = 1.386 Canadian Dollars)
